digest.component_or_area: plan-review gate / completion verifier / attestation validation
propositions: A repository-provable acceptance criterion tagged [operator-attested] was incorrectly accepted at close because the LLM evidence-kind judgment missed the repo path citation and the provenance-line lint (P6) was only advisory, leaving no deterministic blocking guard.

The completion verifier accepts tagged ACs at face value per ADR-0043 design, so the blocking rejection must occur on the close path before the verifier runs, via a deterministic pre-LLM guard that fires on tagged ACs citing exact repo paths/symbols.

A new detector (det_attestation_launder.py) with precision matchers (repo-root-anchored paths, code-extension slash paths, pytest ::node ids, test_* symbols) identifies laundering via [operator-attested] ACs whose own block text cites repo evidence, deliberately excluding commit SHAs and Gerrit numbers (which are legitimate attestation-event provenance).

Tagged ACs missing provenance: continuation lines must be rejected at close; the advisory P6 lint is promoted to blocking on the close path only via ensure_attested_items_valid, maintaining review-side advisory posture per contract.

Mixed-evidence ACs (test file + external outcome) fire the laundering detector and are coached to split into an untagged repo-verifiable criterion and a separately tagged external-evidence criterion with provenance line.

The close precheck ensure_attested_items_valid reports laundering violations before provenance gaps, and both block messages document that edits stale the signed plan-review attestation and require re-running rebar review-plan.
